name: hp-headset-flash
why: A headset with a 3 s hit flash: every hit plays the flash, except the hit that fires the low-health alert. The alert goes out while the previous flash's rest step is still pending, and cancels it.
source: app/test/engine.test.mjs headset hit flash tests (A11.6, polish 2026-09-04); app/src/engine.js `_onHp`

stage_ignores.why: DIVERGENCE: the stage has no gun audio queue model (engine.js `_gun.freeAt`, `_audioSync`). The engine drops a clip that would wait more than PAIN_STALE_MS behind a playing one, and holds the low-health line until the gun is quiet (F375); the stage plays the clip at once. Porting needs the audio model and the sound-duration table.

DIVERGENCE: the stage has no gun audio queue model (engine.js `_gun.freeAt`, `_audioSync`). The engine drops a clip that would wait more than PAIN_STALE_MS behind a playing one, and holds the low-health line until the gun is quiet (F375); the stage plays the clip at once. Porting needs the audio model and the sound-duration table.

Harness timing: the stage runs on an instant `sleep` and spawns at the runner's t=0, the engine spawns later, so a headset write that follows a hold (hit flash, low-health line) or the 5 s F68 periodic repaint (its frame equals the hit rest frame) lands at a different checkpoint. The hit-time re-send itself is pinned in test_stage.py.

The stage has no HUD moment slot to expose as state (its `_moment` is an internal gate); the HUD reads the engine's.
The stage keeps no death count (MC and the HUD read the engine's); `alive` is compared instead.
The stage has no MC link, so it has no match phase; it is armed and spawned by its own buttons.
